content.title: Permitting process tips
content.summary: Early planning and communication are essential for successful construction projects, as they help clarify permit requirements, project timelines, and potential costs. It's important to understand that building and fire codes may vary by jurisdiction, and verifying compliance of materials before installation can prevent delays. Engaging with City staff for guidance and selecting licensed contractors with proper insurance can further support a smooth permitting and construction process.
content.body:
Construction projects are a collaborative effort involving property owners, contractors, design professionals and City staff. While every project is unique, early planning, communication and coordination can help support a smoother permitting and construction experience from start to finish.

## Plan ahead to understand requirements

Successful projects often begin with early planning and coordination. Taking time upfront to understand permit requirements, gather needed documents, and communicate with your project team can help reduce delays and unexpected issues later in the process.

Early coordination can help clarify:

- Applicable code requirements
- Permit and inspection processes
- Required documentation
- Project timelines
- Potential impacts to scheduling and costs

Our team is always happy to answer questions early in the process to help support successful projects.

## Be aware that requirements may vary by jurisdiction

Building, fire, and wildfire code requirements may differ between cities and counties based on locally adopted codes and amendments. A project approach that worked in another jurisdiction may require adjustments here.

Checking local requirements early and coordinating with City staff can help avoid delays and support a smoother review process.

## Understand building and fire codes

Building, fire, and wildfire codes are adopted to help protect public safety, property, and community resilience. These requirements establish minimum safety standards for construction projects.

Codes are also designed to allow flexibility and innovation. There are often multiple ways to achieve compliance depending on the project design and construction approach.

For unique designs, materials, or construction methods, applicants may request consideration through an [Alternative Means and Methods process](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1239/Guidelines-for-Alternate-Materials-Metho), which allows the Building or Fire Code Official to evaluate proposed alternatives for equivalent compliance and safety.

## Keep permit scheduling and budgeting in mind

Permitting, plan review, and inspections are important parts of the construction process and should be considered as part of overall project scheduling.

Including these steps in project planning early on can help:

- Coordinate subcontractors more effectively
- Align procurement and construction schedules
- Reduce project interruptions
- Support smoother inspections and approvals

## Plan for project costs early

In addition to construction costs, projects may also include:

- Permit fees
- Use tax
- Plan review fees
- Costs of testing, reports, evaluations, and special inspections
- Cost of code-related materials or upgrades

Understanding these potential costs early in the process can help support more accurate budgeting and project planning.

## Verify products and materials before installation

Not all products or materials available for purchase meet adopted code requirements. Confirming compliance before installation can help avoid delays, rework, or replacement costs later in the project.

If questions arise about a specific material or product, our team may be able to help provide guidance on applicable requirements.

## Be thoughtful when selecting a contractor

Before hiring a contractor, confirm they hold any required state or local licenses and carry active insurance coverage, including:

- General liability insurance
- Workers’ compensation insurance

Licensed and properly insured contractors help provide protection for both property owners and workers throughout the project.

We suggest taking the following steps when selecting a contractor:

- Research experience
- Compare detailed estimates from multiple contractors
- Use a clearly written contract
- Structure payments around completed project milestones rather than paying the full project cost upfront

## Consider City staff a resource for you

Building and fire officials play an important role in helping projects move safely and successfully through the permitting and inspection process. Open communication and early coordination can often help resolve questions more efficiently and reduce surprises during construction.

If questions come up during planning, permitting, or construction, we encourage you to reach out to our team.

**Remember that collaboration helps projects succeed**. Our shared goal is to support projects that are safe, successful, and beneficial to the community. Strong communication, early coordination, and collaboration between project teams and City staff can help create a smoother experience for everyone involved.

We appreciate the work of the contractors, design professionals, business owners, and residents who help build and improve our community every day!
